title: Evidence oncall procedures and schema notes
body:
Purpose and audience:
This note is an on-call focused runbook + live design sketch for incidents affecting automated evidence capture and SIEM export. Primary audience: oncall engineers in sec-compliance and SRE who need quick triage steps, plus engineering leads who will update schema/permissions after an incident.

Scope:
- Collector failures (backoff, OOM, misconfig, credential rotation)
- Evidence routing mismatches (wrong TTL, dropped artifacts)
- SIEM export lag or schema rejection errors (mapping failures, field truncation)
- RBAC v2 permission regressions that break evidence pickup or export
- Safe remediation steps and temporary mitigations to preserve chain-of-custody

Quick triage checklist (first 10min):
1) Confirm alert details: alert name, sample event id, pipeline shard, and time window.
2) Identify if this is collector-side or export-side: check collector logs (collector-*/stdout) for 5xx or rate-limit logs; check export worker logs for mapping/rejection errors.
3) If suspicious RBAC error observed (403 / permission denied to ingest/export endpoint), escalate to sec-admin and rotate to a fallback service account with minimal write scope.
4) If backlog is growing: enable backpressure mode (see step: enable-backpressure).
5) If evidence TTL is approaching and export blocked, trigger temporary archival (s3:/evidence-hold/<incident-id>) with metadata tags for later replay.

Useful commands (k8s + gcloud examples):
- kubectl -n evidence logs -l app=evidence-collector --since=30m | grep "error"
- gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=evidence-exporter@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $(TOKEN)" https://evidence-internal.redwood/api/v1/ping

Safe mitigation patterns (fast and reversible):
- Fallback SA swap: replace exporter SA with a pre-provisioned readonly-ish SA that has write-only to archive bucket but not to production SIEM. Use this to drain backlog to archive.
- Throttle exporters: set exporter concurrency to 2 and reduce batch size to 50 to avoid downstream rejection floods.
- Toggle schema-strict-mode: set SIEM_EXPORT_STRICT=false to allow fuzzy-mapping for immediate throughput; must be followed by a quality sweep.
- Pause non-critical evidence categories (e.g., telemetry-debug) while preserving security controls evidence.

RBAC v2 incident checklist:
- Verify permission audit: run permission-checker against the service account and the collector role binding.
- If role-bound subject is missing, check gitops repo for recent RBAC PRs (repo: infra/rbac). Roll back to last known-good binding if needed.
- Log all RBAC changes into the evidence incident ticket for audit trail.

Schema and SIEM mapping quick reference:
- Required fields for control-evidence: evidence_id (uuid), control_id, capture_ts (ISO8601), source_node, md5_hash, proof_location (s3 path), retention_ttl_days (int), rw_status (enum: collected|staged|exported|archived).
- Common rejection reasons: field-length > 1024 (trim message fields), unexpected null for required enum, timestamp outside allowed window (>30d in future or <1970).
- When receiving "mapping_missing_field: control_id": run the schema-compat tool to produce a shim: schema-shim --add-field control_id:string --default unknown. This creates a temporary transform layer in the export pipeline.

Evidence preservation play (if export failing > 1h):
- Create incident bucket: gsutil mb gs://evidence-hold-<incident>-<date> && set lifecycle to 365d 
- Create manifest file manifest-<incident>.ndjson that lists per-evidence metadata lines (one JSON per line). Use collector bulk-export: collector admin export --since 2025-02-14 --out manifest-<incident>.ndjson --include-metadata
- Ship manifest + blobs to secure archive and mark chain_of_custody=true in metadata.

Monitoring and dashboards to check quickly:
- Evidence pipeline lag (p50/p95/p99) per category and per shard
- Export rejection rate by error class (mapping, auth, network)
- RBAC permission change events (audit log feed) correlated to deploy times
- SIEM endpoint 4xx/5xx rates and average batch size

Post-incident recovery flow (30–90min window):
1) Stabilize: apply one of the safe mitigations to stop loss.
2) Rehydrate: if backlog archived, rehydrate to staging SIEM and run subset verification (1000 events) against expected queries.
3) Root cause: if RBAC, link to git PR/merge and determine whether change was intended; if schema, identify the PR that introduced breaking field changes.
4) Postmortem: file a blameless incident report, include: timeline, actions taken, retained evidence bucket link, and an action owner for each remediation item.

Operational improvements and open items (actionable):
- [ ] Add a \"safe-mode\" feature toggle on agents to automatically reduce batch size on repeated 4xx for 5 minutes. Owner: Marcus Nguyen. ETA: Q1 2025.
- [ ] Add synthetic evidence tests to pre-deploy pipeline that validate SIEM mapping for critical controls. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: Q2 2025.
- [ ] Create an RBAC canary detector that alerts when a role-binding for collector/extractor changes outside of the gitops PR flow. Owner: Security Automation.
- [ ] Define retention escalation policy when TTL would expire before export completes (auto-extend + notify compliance).

Notes from last incident (2024-10-21):
- Root cause: schema-lint rules in downstream SIEM were updated without compatibility shim.
- Mitigation used: toggled schema-strict-mode=false and archived 12k events.
- Gaps found: no automated test for field length changes; no privileged rollback SA documented.

Questions for follow-up design session:
- Do we need dual-writing (SIEM + archive) at source to avoid single export point failures? Tradeoffs: cost & duplicate deduplication complexity.
- Should we offer pre-provisioned emergency SAs per region? Who owns rotation?
- What is the exact audit evidence schema that product teams expect for compliance controls (finalize on Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC-EVID-42).

Appendix: quick debug examples
- Example transform to truncate long messages: 
  jq '.message = (.message | if length > 1024 then .[:1024] + \"…TRUNC\" else . end)' event.json > event-trunc.json

- Minimal evidence metadata example (newline-delimited JSON as a single string here):
  {"evidence_id":"8f14e45f-ea2a-4b2e-9c3b-1f3a9a2b0c3d","control_id":"C-123","capture_ts":"2025-02-14T15:22:10Z","source_node":"collector-7","md5_hash":"d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e","proof_location":"gs://evidence-hold-incident/8f14..json","retention_ttl_days":"90","rw_status":"staged"}

Contact matrix (who to page):
- Evidence collectors: pager oncall-evidence (primary)
- Exporters/SIEM: pager oncall-siem (primary)
- RBAC and IAM: pager oncall-iam (primary)
- Compliance lead (non-pager): Priya Shah

Sign-off and next steps:
- Circulate this draft to oncall + sec automation leads before end of sprint for feedback.
- Convert checklist items into Jira tasks and link back to this doc in the ticket.

---
